result.rationale: The diff shows removeMember calling self.findMembers() with no offset adjustment. On the frontend, next/previous clamp offset, but removeMember does not; if the only member on the last page is removed, findMembers runs with a stale offset (clamped only against the pre-removal user_count), and the server-side members endpoint applies offset without clamping, so an empty page can result. The mechanism is plausible but exact off-by-one behavior isn't fully verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Discourse.Group.removeMember`, after a successful DELETE it calls `self.findMembers()` without adjusting pagination state. `findMembers` computes the request offset as `Math.min(this.get("user_count"), this.get("offset"))`. If you are on the last page and delete the last member such that `user_count` decreases enough that the current `offset` is now at/after the end (e.g. total 51, limit 50, offset 50 -> delete one => total 50), `user_count` is still the old value when `findMembers` runs, so it will request `offset=50`. The server (`GroupsController#members`) applies `limit/offset` directly and will return an empty `members` array for `offset == total`, leaving the UI on an empty page. This is a verifiable correctness issue introduced by the diff; offset needs clamping (e.g. to `max(0, total-limit)`) before reloading, or after seeing an empty page.
